name: First-Time Setup — Connect with create-app
query: I want to start using Conductor but I don't have anything set up yet
expected_behavior: Step 1: Resolve the CLI per Rule 3 (`ensure-cli.sh` accepts any `conductor`); right before `create-app`, run it with `--need create-app`, asking before installing anything; use the printed `CONDUCTOR_BIN` for every later command

Step 2: Run `conductor config list`. No profiles and no server named → use Developer Edition (`https://developer.orkescloud.com`, profile `developer`) and say so in one line, inviting a URL for another server

Step 3: Run `conductor create-app --server https://developer.orkescloud.com --profile developer` itself, with a long timeout, and tell the user to sign in and click **Approve** when the browser opens (after the CLI's `Opening <url>` line, or conditionally beforehand). No key or secret is typed, pasted or printed
Step 4: Verify with `conductor --profile developer whoami` and `conductor --profile developer workflow list --json`

Step 5: If create-app fails `no_launchpad`, or times out with the browser on another machine, use the manual key path: the user creates a key (or uses the printed `?setup=key` link) and runs interactive `conductor config save --profile developer` in their own terminal
success_criteria: Connection uses `conductor create-app` run by the agent; sending the user to create an access key in the UI and save it with `config save` as the main path fails this criterion (it is only the `no_launchpad` / timeout fallback)
Developer Edition is the default only because no profiles exist and no server was named, and the agent says so
No `localhost` profile or local server is set up unasked
Credential values never enter chat, agent tool input, command arguments, clipboard reads, or raw-profile inspection
Verification uses a real authenticated call with `--profile developer`
